name: 1. Month-end 60/40 Calendar-rebalancing fade (HMM timing, ZN-based signal), MES
primary_rule: DATA TO BUY: ZN (10-yr T-note) from Databento GLBX.MDP3, symbol ZN.v.0 (stype continuous), schema ohlcv-1m, 2010-06-07 to present. Use ohlcv-1h if 1-min is too expensive: the 15:00 ET hourly bar's close is the 16:00 price. Run `PYTHONPATH=./pylib python3 fetch_databento.py cost` first; it already lists 'ZN.v.0 ohlcv-1m 2010-now'. The price is unverified. CALENDAR: T = last NYSE trading day of the month, i.e. the cash_day sessions in data/daily_sessions_ES.pkl. T_prev = the previous month's T. All T-k and T+k offsets count NYSE trading days only. CLOSE = close of the 15:59 ET bar (bars are stamped at their open), i.e. the 16:00 price; on early-close days use the 12:59 bar close. RETURNS: for ES and ZN separately, r_d = (adj_close_d - adj_close_{d-1}) / raw_close_{d-1}. Build adjusted closes with the same additive back-adjustment at the roll minute as daily_sessions.py. ZN uses its 16:00 ET bar price, not its 15:00 ET settlement. SIGNAL on each t in {T-4,...,T}: G_ES = product of (1+r_ES) over d = T_prev+1..t, and G_ZN likewise. For day t's own return, use the 15:55 price (close of the 15:54 bar) to avoid look-ahead. Cal_t = sign(G_ES - G_ZN). My algebra: this equals the sign of HMM's Calendar signal w_t - 60%, because the calendar portfolio does not rebalance inside the month, so w_t = 0.6*G_ES/(0.6*G_ES + 0.4*G_ZN). POSITION: hold -Cal_t MES (1 contract) from the close of t to the close of t+1, for t = T-4..T. That means: enter at the T-4 close; at the T-3, T-2, T-1 and T closes, flip if the sign changed; exit at the close of T+1 (first NYSE day of the new month). Flat on all other days. ROLLS: the ES quarterly roll (about 8 days before the 3rd Friday) never falls in T-4..T+1, because T-4 is on or after the 22nd. Assert instrument_id is constant over the hold; if it is not, book each leg within one contract. HOLIDAYS: days the NYSE is closed (Globex-only sessions, Good Friday, Oct 29-30 2012, national days of mourning; the last two from memory, unverified) are neither counted nor traded; the position is carried through them. COSTS: per contract per side, 1 tick (0.25 pt = $1.25) + $0.50 commission. A round trip costs $3.50 (= 0.70 index pt); a flip trades 2 contracts. Stress test at 2 ticks/side. Report P&L in $ per MES (ES points x $5) and in bp of the raw entry price. If ZN is not bought, run the same rule with Cal_t = sign(G_ES - 1) as a labelled weak fallback, not as a variant.
variants: (a) Add HMM's reversal leg: at the T+1 close switch to +Cal_{T-4} MES and exit at the T+2 close. Section 4 sets the first business day's weight to sign(Calendar Signal_{-4}), applied to the next day's return.
(b) Primary rule on MNQ (NQ prices, $2/pt; round trip $2.00 = 1.00 NQ pt at 1 tick/side). No source tests the Nasdaq-100, so report it separately and never use it to rescue the MES result.
evaluation: In-paper overlap: 152 month-ends, Jul 2010 to Feb 2023. June 2010 is skipped because the prior month-end close is missing. Post-paper: 44 month-ends, Mar 2023 to Oct 2026. The authors' own extension runs to 2025, so only 2026 is untouched by them. Statistic: net P&L per event. PASS requires all of the following. (1) Full-sample net mean > 0 with event-level t >= 2.0 (one pre-registered test). (2) Post-paper net mean > 0 (sign check only; SE reported). (3) Signal spread: the mean ES return over T-4 close to T+1 close in months with Cal_{T-4} < 0 minus that in months with Cal_{T-4} > 0 is positive. This shows the edge is not turn-of-month drift. (4) The repo gates in preregistration.md: net mean > 0 in at least 2/3 of 2-year blocks, gross mean >= 1.5x round-trip cost, and still > 0 after removing Feb-Mar 2020. Diagnostics, not trials: (i) split by trailing 20-day ES realized vol above or below its expanding median, because HMM Table 6 shows 16.50% vs 3.91% p.a. for high vs low VIX; (ii) P&L by month of quarter; (iii) P&L on days T and T+1 separately. Trials: 3 (primary + 2 variants).
source_sample_end: 2023-03-17. Footnote 32 says 'extended the sample through 2025' with 'even stronger' results (untabulated). The reviewer read the authors' Feb 2026 slides: 1997-2025 cross-asset Calendar x week4 = -0.2849 (SE 0.0779).

name: 2. Pre-expiry overnight long: close of the day before monthly options expiry to the 09:30 open on expiry, MES
primary_rule: EVENT DAY E: the monthly SPX expiry. That is the 3rd Friday, or, when that Friday is an NYSE holiday, the last NYSE trading day before it in the same week. Use calendar_days.expiry_fridays() on cash_day sessions, the same calendar as strategy 3. Examples by my calendar arithmetic, to verify: Good Friday on 2014-04-18, 2019-04-19, 2022-04-15 and 2025-04-18 moves E to Thursday, and Juneteenth on 2026-06-19 moves E to 2026-06-18. DPB footnote 2 treats its 4 holiday cases the same way. ENTRY: buy 1 MES at the close of the 15:59 ET bar on the NYSE trading day immediately before E (normally the 3rd Thursday). EXIT: sell at the open of the 09:30 ET bar on E. CONTRACT: whatever the volume-roll series holds at the entry bar. In Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec the roll about 8 days earlier means this is already the next quarterly contract, so both legs are in it and the expiring contract is never traded. DPB footnote 13: using the next-to-delivery contract on quarterly dates gives 'very similar results'. Assert the same instrument_id at entry and exit; otherwise skip the event and log it. HOLIDAY SPANS: if a non-NYSE day falls between entry and E, keep the event but flag it, and report results with and without flagged events. Example: Juneteenth Thursday 2025-06-19 before E = 2025-06-20, so entry is Wed 2025-06-18. COSTS: 1 tick/side + $1 round trip = $3.50 (0.70 pt). Both fills are at RTH boundaries, but because the 09:30 fill is fast, the pass rule also requires net > 0 at 2 ticks/side ($6.00 = 1.20 pt).
variants: (a) Same rule on MNQ (NQ prices, $2/pt; $2.00 round trip at 1 tick/side, $3.00 at 2 ticks/side).
evaluation: In-paper overlap: 139 events, Jun 2010 to Dec 2021. Post-paper: 58 events, Jan 2022 to Oct 2026. The Nov 20 2026 expiry has not happened yet. BENCHMARK: all other NYSE nights in the same period, measured from the 15:59 close to the next 09:30 open, excluding pre-expiry nights. Excess = event return minus the benchmark mean. PASS requires all of the following. (1) Full-sample mean gross excess with t >= 2.0. (2) Post-paper mean net (1 tick) > 0 and post-paper mean excess > 0, as a sign check. (3) Full-sample net mean > 0 at 2 ticks/side. (4) The repo gates. Power, by my arithmetic from DPB's SD of 60.53 bp: SE is about 8 bp on 58 post-paper events and about 4.3 bp on 197 events. The in-paper excess of about 11.6 bp (14.30 - 2.69) would give only t of about 1.5 post-paper. Diagnostics, not trials: (i) quarterly vs off-quarterly split (the quarterly +26/-37 bp figures are SOQ-based and not tradable); (ii) the average 1-min cumulative path from 16:00 to 12:00 for 2010-2021 vs 2022-2026, to see whether the peak moved; (iii) correlation with strategy 3 P&L on the same E, and results split by overnight return >= 0 vs < 0. Trials: 2.

name: 3. Settlement-aligned month-end liquidity reversal (dash for cash), MES long
primary_rule: T, closes, holidays and costs follow spec 1. Settlement lag k = 3 for trade dates before 2017-09-05, 2 for 2017-09-05 to 2024-05-27, and 1 from 2024-05-28. L = the last NYSE trading day whose sale settles on or before T-1. With k taken from L's own date, that is L = T-(k+1): T-4 in the T+3 era, T-3 in T+2, T-2 in T+1. Worked cases: Aug 2017 gives L = Aug 25; Sep 2017 gives L = Sep 26; May 2024 gives L = May 29. ENTRY: buy 1 MES at the 15:59-bar close of L. EXIT: sell at the 15:59-bar close of T-1 (12:59 bar on early-close days). The hold is 3, 2 or 1 sessions by regime. The rule is unconditional. No roll can fall inside, since L is on or after the 22nd. Costs: 1 tick/side + $1 ($3.50 round trip); both fills are at the RTH close.
variants: (a) Filter on Etula's -0.38 correlation: trade only when S < 0, where S = (ES 15:55 price on L) / (15:59 close of L-5) - 1.

(b) Mechanism control: use Etula's fixed window in every month (enter at the T-4 close, exit at the T-1 close). Before 2017-09 it is identical to the primary. The settlement mechanism is supported only if the primary beats (b) over Sep 2017 to Oct 2026.
evaluation: In-paper overlap: 43 events, Jun 2010 to Dec 2013. Post-paper: 154 events, Jan 2014 to Oct 2026, split by regime: T+3 44 (to Aug 2017), T+2 80 (Sep 2017 to Apr 2024), T+1 30 (May 2024 to Oct 2026). BENCHMARK: the mean of all h-session close-to-close windows in the same calendar year (h = the event's hold length) that start outside T-8..T+3 of every month. Excess = event return minus benchmark; a long-only window earns ordinary drift, so raw P&L is not evidence. PASS requires all of the following. (1) Post-paper mean net excess > 0 with t >= 2.0 (one pre-registered test). (2) Net excess > 0 in at least 2 of the 3 settlement regimes. (3) The repo gates. Report variant (b) beside the primary for Sep 2017 onward. Expect a fail under decay: by the reviewer's arithmetic, even full in-sample strength (about 25 bp abnormal) gives t of only about 1.8. Do not scan entry days D-1 and D+1. Trials: 3.

name: 4. Turn-of-month day+1 long (tom+1): control, not a deployment candidate
primary_rule: Buy 1 MES at the 15:59-bar close of T, the last NYSE trading day of the month. On an early-close T, use the 12:59 bar instead; by my calendar arithmetic that applies to 2019-11-29, 2024-11-29 and 2025-11-28. Sell at the 15:59-bar close of T+1, the first NYSE trading day of the new month. Report the overnight leg (T close to T+1 09:30-bar open) and the intraday leg (09:30-bar open to 15:59 close of T+1) separately. No roll falls inside. Costs: 1 tick/side + $1 ($3.50 round trip).
variants: (a) Intraday leg only as the trade: buy at the 09:30-bar open of T+1 and sell at its 15:59-bar close. This is the leg that pit-era sources found carried the effect.
evaluation: All 197 events (Jun 2010 to Oct 2026) are after the source samples. BENCHMARK: all other close-to-close days in the same period (open-to-close days for variant a). PASS: mean net excess > 0 with t >= 2.0, plus the repo gates. Post-2006 retests (QuanterLab, QuantSeeker, ATB) predict a fail. Purpose: if it passes, spec 1's T to T+1 day and spec 1 variant (a) must be re-estimated net of a tom+1 dummy. Trials: 2.
